alert.name: ECSServiceAlarm
alert.summary: CloudWatch alarm fired for ECS service checkout

root_cause.hypothesis: Alarm fired during a transient state of an in-progress rolling deployment/task replacement (deployments_in_flight=1): new task <TASK_2> started and went healthy while old task <TASK_1> was still running and heartbeating, briefly showing two task IDs active. No actual outage: tasks_running matches tasks_desired (2/2), tasks_pending=0, deployments_failed=0, CPU/memory nominal, and both task IDs heartbeat continuously with no gaps or errors in logs. RECENT DEPLOYS being empty despite deployments_in_flight=1 is unexplained â€” the trigger for this task replacement (deploy, scale event, manual force-new-deployment, or health-check-driven task cycling) isn't identified in the evidence.
evidence: tasks_running == tasks_desired (2.0 == 2.0), tasks_pending=0 â€” no capacity shortfall
CPU 0.5%, memory 65% â€” no resource exhaustion
Logs show <TASK_1> and <TASK_2> both heartbeating 'ok' continuously, no error/unhealthy lines
<TASK_2> starts healthy at 05:23:18 while <TASK_1> still heartbeats until 05:25:20 â€” overlap consistent with rolling replacement
deployments_in_flight=1 confirms a deployment/task-replacement was active at alarm time
ruled_out: Task crash loop / failure â€” no unhealthy or stopped events in logs
Resource exhaustion (CPU/memory) â€” both well below typical thresholds
Stuck pending tasks â€” tasks_pending=0 throughout

proposal.reasoning: 2/2 tasks running, 0 pending, 0 failed deploys, cpu/mem nominal. Two task IDs = transient rolling replacement overlap, both heartbeating clean throughout. No error/gap in logs. Alarm self-resolves once old task drains.
proposal.expected_effect: No change. Alarm clears when deployment_in_flight completes and single task ID remains.
